newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates rise on NCD issue, bond auction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates rise on NCD issue, bond auction.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates rose at mid-session on Tuesday, with liquidity tightening on the central bank's issue of T$3 billion negotiable certificates of deposit, dealers said.
Operations also have turned cautious prior to the finance ministry's scheduled T$15 billion government bond auction later this afternoon, dealers added.

At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 7.255 percent against Monday's 6.931 percent close -- far outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 7.25-7.35 percent against 6.50-6.75.
Dealers said the money rates also faced rising pressure due to the continued exodus of funds into the sizzling stock market.
The stock market, hit by heavy profit-taking following a recent bull charge, slumped 2.88 percent on Tuesday to close at 9,550.40. Turnover was extremely heavy at T$206 billion.
Dealers said they expected the rates to continue rising on the various aforementioned liquidity-squeezing factors.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9600-9625 percent against 5.9675.
